core_en: Identity forms in a loop: goal → attention → action → habit → “this is who I am” → defending it. To change, break the loop between habit and defence.
core_zh: 身份是这样形成的：目标 → 注意力 → 行动 → 习惯 → “我就是这种人” → 拼命维护它。想改变，就要在“习惯”和“维护”之间打断这个循环。

diagram.caption_en: The identity loop. The key step is not more effort — it is to stop defending the old identity without question.
diagram.caption_zh: 身份循环。改变的关键一步不是更努力，而是停止无条件维护旧身份。

label: Chapter 03 · 身份受到威胁时

paragraphs.en: As a child, you needed your parents to survive, so you learned to act in ways they approved of. Later, you also need a social identity that other people respect. So you hold on to labels — a job title, a belief, a group — as if your life depends on it.
paragraphs.zh: 小时候，你需要父母才能生存，所以你学会按他们认可的方式行动。长大后，你还需要一个受人尊重的社会身份。于是你紧紧抓住各种标签 —— 职业、信仰、圈子 —— 好像命都系在上面。

paragraphs.en: That is why a challenge to your identity can feel like a physical threat. Your body goes into fight-or-flight, and you defend yourself instead of listening. The same feeling appears when you try to change: the old identity fights to stay alive.
paragraphs.zh: 所以，当身份受到挑战时，感觉就像身体受到威胁一样。你会进入“战斗或逃跑”模式，急着反驳，而不是倾听。想改变时也一样：旧身份会拼命挣扎着活下去。

title_en: Fear keeps your old identity alive
title_zh: 你不是不想变，你是害怕变

vocab.def_zh: 条件反射式的习惯养成；长期训练形成的行为模式。
vocab.example_en: Years of conditioning made it automatic.
vocab.example_zh: 多年的习惯养成让它变成了自动反应。

vocab.def_zh: 战斗或逃跑反应：感到威胁时身体的本能反应。
vocab.example_en: Criticism put him in fight-or-flight mode.
vocab.example_zh: 批评让他进入了战斗或逃跑模式。

vocab.def_zh: 顺从；迎合；遵守（规则/期待）。
vocab.example_en: As a kid, I conformed to fit in.
vocab.example_zh: 小时候，我为了融入大家而顺从。

vocab.example_en: It was a psychological need, not a physical one.
vocab.example_zh: 那是心理上的需要，不是身体上的。
